leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye, all with the same two names and citations that differ only in wording (Kroll and Pearce stress the 10^-18 regime; Olsson adds trapping at the magic wavelength; Lindroth stresses accuracy and stability). They share the view that the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, that the work is mature and reproduced in many laboratories, and that it is distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion control prizes. What is not shared is how far each treats it as a discovery rather than an instrument advance: Lindroth and Olsson both record that it may be seen as metrological refinement, and Kroll flags the lineage overlap. All four list the tail of unnamed contributors (Lemonde, Takamoto, Yb and Hg groups) as an open credit question, and Kroll discloses a Hall-laboratory tie that bears on this ballot.

Three members prefer the topological-insulator ballot with the same Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio and a citation built on the quantum spin Hall effect, its first observation and band topology as an organising principle. Johansson and Mehlig each moved to this trio from other opening configurations (Kane and Molenkamp; Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan) after reading the openings. They share the argument that the interpretation is stable after fifteen to twenty years and that the 2016 prize covered distinct physics. They also all state that the credit remains incomplete: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, with Zhang deceased, sits outside the credited names, and the 3D and quantum anomalous Hall strands are left out. They differ in how heavily to weigh that gap, and Johansson names B022 as a clean fallback.

Only Danielsson prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene for MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, as a sharp prediction followed by an unexpected experiment that opened a large field. No other member put it in their preferred configuration, but it is a named alternative of Eriksson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, so it has the widest second-choice support. Danielsson accepts that the pairing mechanism is unsettled and that Cao, Fatemi and other groups are outside the credited names; the other members who comment treat timing, not merit, as the obstacle.

areas_of_agreement: All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes drawn from three ballots (B022, B045, B030); no member prefers a multi-part split or any of the quantum-information, cosmology or neutrino ballots.

Everyone who comments accepts the scientific merit of all three leading ballots; the disagreement is about maturity, attribution and the kind of achievement, not about whether the work is significant.
Every member who proposes B045 uses the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio, and every member who proposes B022 uses Katori and Ye, so within each ballot the names are not contested among supporters.

Johansson and Mehlig both concede that Xue's quantum anomalous Hall effect is a later and distinct step, and Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson are explicit that B004 mixes it with the quantum spin Hall effect.

Members on both sides state that any topological-insulator prize omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and that any lattice-clock prize omits other clock pioneers; both gaps are acknowledged by supporters and sceptics alike.
scientific_disputes: Whether a record-precision lattice clock is a discovery or invention of the kind the statute describes, or a refinement of the lineage honoured in 2005 and 2012 (raised by Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce in their statements or responses; Olsson and Pearce reply that it opens a new measurement regime).

Whether the Z2 classification and protected edge states of time-reversal-invariant insulators are distinct enough from the 2016 topological-phases prize (Eriksson, Johansson and Lindroth say yes; Danielsson, Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce raise the overlap).

Whether the conceptual breadth of topological band theory (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, and acknowledged by Pearce) should weigh more than a clean, instrument-level result with demonstrated downstream tests of constants and redshift (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce).

Whether the origin of the correlated and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene is settled enough to treat it as a stable discovery (Danielsson says the flat-band origin is stable; Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce emphasise that the pairing mechanism and sensitivity to twist-angle disorder are unresolved).
attribution_disputes: B045 supporters differ with the B004 and earlier opening proposals on the third name: Hasan (opening Danielsson, Mehlig) or Xue (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson on B004) versus Mele (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig after round 1, Pearce). Johansson would accept Kane and Molenkamp only as a B004 fallback.

The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal, which directed Molenkamp's experiment, is outside the credited names and Zhang is deceased; Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson all raise it, with Olsson treating it as a fairness cost against B045 and the B045 supporters proposing to address it in the wording of the citation.

For B022, Lemonde, Takamoto, Hollberg, Derevianko, the Yb and Hg groups and Ye's JILA collaborators are unnamed (raised by Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce); Lindroth and Pearce ask how credit divides between Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's realisation, and Pearce notes the contest between the Katori and Ye groups over the 10^-18 regime.
For B030, Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Young, Santos, Lopes dos Santos and other groups are outside the credited names, and Danielsson asks whether a three-person limit can fairly omit them.
maturity_disputes: B030 is called early by Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce (about seven to eight years after 2018, unsettled mechanism, disorder sensitivity); Danielsson and Johansson do not regard the unfinished theory of the phases as disqualifying.

B022 is described as mature and reproduced by its supporters, but the redefinition of the SI second has not occurred; Kroll and Pearce consider it not a precondition, while Mehlig and Olsson ask whether its timing would strengthen the case.

B045 is called mature and arguably overdue by Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig, while Danielsson, Kroll and Pearce point to the 2016 prize as a possible reason for caution; Mehlig adds that applications are still mostly prospective.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll (B022): documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Jun Ye is a Hall-lineage JILA scientist. Kroll notes no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye and says the committee may need to consider recusal.

Johansson (B039): directs WACQT at Chalmers, has a documented link to Chalmers colleagues such as Per Delsing, and says he would recuse himself from deciding B039; he reports no conflict on the topological-insulator ballots.
Olsson (B039): shares Chalmers with Johansson and suggests a Chalmers link to the circuit-QED community be considered if B039 is discussed; no effect on B022.

Eriksson (B045): electronic-structure and materials-theory group at Uppsala is adjacent to the topological-materials theme; no personal or institutional tie to the credited names is documented and no recusal is proposed.
Lindroth (B022): general disciplinary closeness to atomic and precision physics, stated as a bias rather than a formal conflict; no documented tie to Katori, Ye or any credited name.

Pearce (chair, B046 and B002): documented astroparticle collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO) could become relevant if IceCube neutrinos or baryon acoustic oscillations were taken up; the chair reports no conflict on B022, B045 or B030.
questions_for_round2: For B022: Is the committee satisfied that lattice clocks are a discovery or invention distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and can the citation be worded around the magic-wavelength lattice architecture and the 10^-18 regime so as not to cover optical clocks in general?
For B022: How should credit be divided between Katori's concept and Ye's realisation, and is a two-name prize defensible given Lemonde, Takamoto and the Yb and Hg groups?

For B022: Does the pending redefinition of the SI second strengthen the case, or does Kroll's recusal question (Hall-laboratory stay) change how the committee should weigh Kroll's and the other B022 positions?

For B045: Can the citation be limited to the prediction and first observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification so as to stand without the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, the 3D strand (Hasan) and the quantum anomalous Hall strand (Xue)?

For B045: Does the 2016 prize on topological phases make a second topology prize premature, given that Eriksson, Johansson and Lindroth argue the physics is distinct while Danielsson, Kroll and Pearce see it as a close follow-up?

For B030: What would the committee need to see on the origin of the correlated and superconducting states, and is there a fair way to credit Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero without Cao, Fatemi and the other experimental groups?

Across ballots: Between a mature, cleanly attributed instrument-level result (B022) and a broader conceptual result with an incomplete credit tree (B045), which criterion should decide, and how does each member weigh breadth of influence against attribution clarity?
Should Kroll's Hall-lineage connection and Johansson's and Olsson's Chalmers links lead to formal recusal on B022 or B039 respectively, or are they to be handled as disclosed bias?
summary.chair_observation: Explicit round-1 positions are four members for B022, three for B045 and one for B030; no other ballot is a preferred configuration. The B022 and B045 groups each find the other a credible alternative, while B030 is the most frequent named alternative and is mainly held back on maturity. The question that appears to separate the groups is how to weigh a clean attribution and mature interpretation against breadth of conceptual influence, and round 2 should test whether the citation wording can answer the remaining credit objections on each ballot.
